summary: This bill amends the Social Security Act to change how Medicare pays for certain surgical procedures with high-cost supplies when performed in office-based facilities, making the payment similar to how ambulatory surgical centers are paid for these procedures, starting in 2027.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Social Security Act to adjust Medicare payment rules for certain surgical procedures performed in office-based facilities. It aims to align payment for high-cost supply surgical procedures with those performed in ambulatory surgical centers, which directly impacts how healthcare providers are reimbursed under Medicare. This is a significant change to Medicare's payment structure for specific procedures.

The bill adjusts Medicare payment methodology for specified high-cost surgical procedures in office-based facilities (setting facility payments at 90% of ASC rates with device-intensive adjustments and copay caps), which is likely to increase federal Medicare outlays without any offsetting savings provisions.

The legislation expands government-set Medicare payment rules and facility standards to new office-based settings while capping patient coinsurance at the inpatient deductible level, representing targeted government intervention in provider reimbursement and patient cost-sharing.
